extraValues.description: Free-form values referenced from templated strings in cluster.spec (and labels/annotations).

spec.description: ValkeyCluster.spec. Unknown keys are rejected: put fields this chart does not cover in cluster.additionalSpec.

acl.description: ACL configures the Valkey access control the operator manages.

items.description: ACLUserSpec defines a Valkey ACL user.

patterns.description: Pub/Sub channel patterns - maps to Valkey: &pattern

commands.description: Valkey command categories, commands, and subcommands restrictions for this user

readOnly.description: Keys restricted to read-only; maps to Valkey: %R~pattern

readWrite.description: Keys on which this user can read, and write; maps to Valkey: ~pattern

writeOnly.description: Keys restricted to write-only; maps to Valkey: %W~pattern

password.description: Password authentication; defaults to the passwords in the Secret <cluster>-users

secret.description: Reference information to a Secret containing user passwords

keys.description:
An array of keys inside the referencing Secret to find passwords; defaults to username
Valkey supports multiple passwords per user for rotation

name.description: Name of the referencing Secret; Defaults to clustername-users

type.description: How the user authenticates with a password

permissions.description: Raw ACL for (additional) permissions. Appended to anything generated.

containers.description: Additional containers or overrides for existing containers, applied using strategic merge patch

args.description: Additional cmdline arguments passed to exporter sidecar container.

enabled.description:
Enable or disable the exporter sidecar container. Unset means enabled
on a ValkeyCluster; a ValkeyNode runs the sidecar only on an explicit
true, which the cluster controller propagates when enabled.

resources.description: Override resource requirements for the exporter container in each pod

securityContext.description: Override the SecurityContext applied to the exporter sidecar container.

imagePullSecrets.description:
ImagePullSecrets is a list of references to Secrets in the same namespace used for
pulling any of the images (Valkey server, metrics exporter, and any additional
containers) from private registries.

networking.description:
Networking groups how clients and peers reach cluster nodes (TLS,
in-cluster discovery announce, per-node Services, and later external access).

clusterDomain.description:
ClusterDomain is the DNS suffix kubelet publishes Service DNS under
(kubelet --cluster-domain). Used when building Hostname announce FQDNs
and the default TLS ServerName. Must match the cluster. Default cluster.local.

discovery.description: Discovery configures in-cluster endpoint announcement after CLUSTER SLOTS.

preferredEndpointType.description:
PreferredEndpointType selects IP (default) or Hostname announcement.
Hostname uses per-pod DNS under the cluster headless Service
(<pod>.<headless>.<namespace>.svc.<clusterDomain>) and requires
workloadType StatefulSet (or the default).

perNodeServices.description:
PerNodeServices opts in to one ClusterIP Service per node.
Omit it to create none. Each Service selects that one pod.
Announce settings are unchanged.

certificates.description: Certificates holds the certificate slots used by the cluster.

server.description:
Server is the node identity presented to clients and peers, and the
trust root for the cluster. The referenced secret must contain:

- `ca.crt`: The certificate authority.
- `tls.crt`: The certificate (or a chain).
- `tls.key`: The private key to the first certificate in the certificate chain.

secretName.description: SecretName is the name of the secret.

clientAuth.description:
ClientAuth configures client certificate authentication. When omitted,
mode defaults to `Optional` and certificateUser defaults to `Disabled`.

ca.description:
CA lists additional trust roots for verifying client certificates, for
clients whose certificates are issued by a different CA than the server
certificate. Each entry names a Secret or a ConfigMap, and the key in it
holding the roots (default `ca.crt`) as PEM certificates or a SPIFFE
trust bundle.

The operator merges the server secret's `ca.crt` with the roots under
each entry's key, in list order and without duplicates, into the
operator-managed `valkey-<cluster>-tls-trust` Secret, and nodes verify clients
and peers against that bundle. The server root always stays in the
bundle, since peers present the server certificate on the cluster bus
and replication links.

The operator re-reads these sources on every reconcile, and nodes reload
a changed bundle live, without a restart. SPIRE's
bundle ConfigMap can be referenced as is, with its key (`bundle.spiffe`
or `bundle.crt`).

items.description:
TrustSource references CA certificates held in a Secret or a ConfigMap.
Exactly one of secretName and configMapName must be set.

configMapName.description:
ConfigMapName is the name of a ConfigMap holding the roots, as SPIRE and
trust-manager publish bundles.

key.description:
Key is the key holding the roots. Defaults to `ca.crt`. Its contents are
either PEM certificates or a SPIFFE trust bundle (a JWK Set, as SPIRE
publishes under `bundle.spiffe`); the operator tells them apart by their
content and, for a SPIFFE bundle, uses the `x5c` certificate of every
key whose `use` is `x509-svid`.

secretName.description:
SecretName is the name of a Secret holding the roots. The Secret type
does not matter.

certificateUser.description:
CertificateUser configures how Valkey maps an authenticated client
certificate to an ACL user. Set to `CN` to use the certificate's Common Name
(requires Valkey >= 9.0), or `URI` to use the first matching URI from the
certificate's Subject Alternative Name (SAN) (requires Valkey >= 9.1).
Defaults to `Disabled`, which leaves the directive unset.

mode.description:
Mode controls whether clients must authenticate with a TLS certificate.
`Required` enforces mTLS, `Optional` allows both authenticated and
unauthenticated clients, and `Disabled` turns client certificate processing
off entirely.
Defaults to `Optional`.

serverName.description:
ServerName is the hostname used for TLS verification when the operator
connects to a node by pod IP. When unset, the operator uses
valkey-<name>.<namespace>.svc.<clusterDomain> (default cluster.local).

persistence.description: Persistence defines durable storage that is propagated to each ValkeyNode.

reclaimPolicy.description:
ReclaimPolicy controls whether the managed PVC is retained or deleted when
the ValkeyNode is deleted. Defaults to Retain.

size.description: Size is the requested PVC size.

storageClassName.description: StorageClassName is the storage class to use for the PVC.

podDisruptionBudget.description:
PodDisruptionBudget configures the operator-managed PodDisruptionBudget(s)
for this cluster. When unset, the operator applies the default (Cluster) mode.

mode.description: Mode selects the PDB strategy. Defaults to Cluster.

podMetadata.description:
PodMetadata adds labels and annotations to every Valkey pod of the cluster.
They are not part of the workload selector, so they can be changed at any
time; a change rolls the pods. Keys the operator sets itself are rejected.

annotations.description:
Annotations added to the object. Values have no format rule, but keys and
values together are limited to 256 KiB less the operator's own annotation.
Keys under valkey.io/ are reserved for the operator.

labels.description:
Labels added to the object. Keys under valkey.io/ and the
app.kubernetes.io/ name, instance, component, part-of and managed-by keys
are reserved for the operator.

podSecurityContext.description:
Override the PodSecurityContext applied to each ValkeyNode pod of the cluster.
When set, this overrides the default PodSecurityContext.

replicas.description:
Deprecated: use replicasPerShard, which has the same meaning. A spec
cannot set both. This field is removed in v1beta1.

replicasPerShard.description: The number of replicas in each shard, in addition to its primary.

resources.description: Override resource requirements for the Valkey container in each pod

scheduling.description:
Scheduling groups pod placement configuration (affinity, node selector,
tolerations, topology spread constraints, priority class) for the
cluster's pods.

affinity.description:
Affinity to apply to the pods. Kubernetes ANDs nodeAffinity with
NodeSelector rather than one overriding the other: a node must satisfy
both for the pod to be scheduled there.

node.description:
Node groups scheduling constraints on the node axis
(topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname). When unset, every node spread is
Disabled and no scheduling primitives are emitted.

spread.description: Spread distributes the cluster's pods across nodes.

pods.description:
Pods balances all of the cluster's pods across nodes, rendered as a
topology spread constraint. Defaults to Disabled when unset. Enabling this
alongside an explicit primaries spread of the same strength is rejected
(only one topology spread constraint per strength is permitted per node).

mode.description:
Mode selects the strength of the constraint. When unset, the dimension's
documented default applies.

primaries.description:
Primaries balances each shard's node-index-0 pod across nodes, rendered as
a topology spread constraint.
Defaults to Disabled when unset.

mode.description:
Mode selects the strength of the constraint. When unset, the dimension's
documented default applies.

shard.description:
Shard keeps pods of the same shard on distinct nodes, rendered as pod
anti-affinity. Defaults to Disabled when unset.

mode.description:
Mode selects the strength of the constraint. When unset, the dimension's
documented default applies.

nodeSelector.description: NodeSelector to apply to the pods

priorityClassName.description:
PriorityClassName is the name of an existing PriorityClass applied to
every pod in the cluster, protecting them from eviction under resource
pressure. Pod priority is a scheduling concern (preemption, scheduling-queue
order), so it lives alongside the other placement fields.

tolerations.description: Tolerations to apply to the pods

topologySpreadConstraints.description: TopologySpreadConstraints to apply to the pods

zone.description:
Zone groups scheduling constraints on the zone axis
(topologyKey topology.kubernetes.io/zone). When unset, every zone spread is
Disabled and no scheduling primitives are emitted.

pinning.description:
Pinning assigns every pod a deterministic zone by round-robin over an
ordered zone list. Mutually exclusive with any non-Disabled Spread field
on this axis: pinning already fixes each pod's zone, so a zone spread
constraint can only contradict it. Unset means no pinning.

zones.description:
Zones is the ordered round-robin sequence. A pod's zone is
zones[(shardIndex + nodeIndex) % len(zones)], so each shard's pods walk
the list from a different starting point, and while there are at least
as many zones as shards, primaries land in distinct zones as a side
effect. When replicasPerShard+1 exceeds the zone count, some members of
a shard necessarily share a zone.

Adding shards or replicas never moves an existing pod, because a pod's
indices never change. Changing this list would move nearly all of them,
so it is immutable while set: remove pinning, reconcile, then re-add it
with the new sequence. On a cluster with persistence, note that zonal
volumes cannot follow a pod to a new zone.

The list is ordered, so it is atomic rather than a set: a set list is
unordered under server-side apply, which would scramble the assignment.
Uniqueness is enforced by CEL for the same reason.

Each entry must be a valid Kubernetes label value, because it is rendered
as the value of a topology.kubernetes.io/zone nodeSelector entry. Without
that constraint an entry such as "eu-west-1a!" is accepted here and then
rejected when the StatefulSet is created, surfacing on the ValkeyNode
rather than on the ValkeyCluster the user edited.

spread.description: Spread distributes the cluster's pods across zones.

pods.description:
Pods balances all of the cluster's pods across zones, rendered as a
topology spread constraint. Defaults to Disabled when unset. Enabling this
alongside an explicit shard or primaries spread of the same strength is
rejected (only one topology spread constraint per strength is permitted per
zone).

mode.description:
Mode selects the strength of the constraint. When unset, the dimension's
documented default applies.

primaries.description:
Primaries balances each shard's node-index-0 pod across zones, rendered as
a topology spread constraint. Defaults to Disabled when unset.

mode.description:
Mode selects the strength of the constraint. When unset, the dimension's
documented default applies.

shard.description:
Shard balances the pods of each shard across zones, rendered as a topology
spread constraint. Defaults to Disabled when unset.

mode.description:
Mode selects the strength of the constraint. When unset, the dimension's
documented default applies.

serviceAccountName.description:
ServiceAccountName specifies the name of the ServiceAccount to use for
ValkeyCluster pods. If unset, the namespace's default ServiceAccount is used.

shards.description: The number of shards groups. Each shard group contains one primary and N replicas.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description:
TerminationGracePeriodSeconds is the pod termination grace period for the
Valkey nodes. It must give the graceful CLUSTER FAILOVER triggered on
SIGTERM (shutdown-on-sigterm) enough time to hand the shard off to a
replica before SIGKILL. When unset, the operator derives a safe default
from cluster-manual-failover-timeout. A value below that derived minimum
is honoured but reported as a warning.

users.description:
Valkey users managed by the operator.

Deprecated: use spec.acl.users; removed in v1beta1.

items.description:
An UserAclSpec contains user, authorization, and permissions-related configurations.
It is the legacy spec.users entry, replaced by ACLUserSpec and removed in v1beta1.

patterns.description: Pub/Sub channel patterns - maps to Valkey: &pattern

commands.description: Valkey command categories, commands, and subcommands restrictions for this user

enabled.description: If the user is enabled or not

readOnly.description: Keys restricted to read-only; maps to Valkey: %R~pattern

readWrite.description: Keys on which this user can read, and write; maps to Valkey: ~pattern

writeOnly.description: Keys restricted to write-only; maps to Valkey: %W~pattern

nopass.description: Do not apply a password to this user

passwordSecret.description: Reference information to a Secret containing user passwords

keys.description:
An array of keys inside the referencing Secret to find passwords; defaults to username
Valkey supports multiple passwords per user for rotation

name.description: Name of the referencing Secret; Defaults to clustername-users

permissions.description: Raw ACL for (additional) permissions. Appended to anything generated.

resetpass.description: Apply the resetpass flag to this user

workloadType.description: WorkloadType specifies whether ValkeyNodes create StatefulSets or Deployments.

additionalSpec.description: ValkeyCluster.spec fields not covered by cluster.spec, deep-merged over it (passed through tpl).
